title: How Long Would You Last on Top of Everest Without Oxygen? #shorts
description_hook: You are teleported to the summit of Everest, 8,848.86 meters up, with no bottled oxygen and no time to acclimatize. The clock starts now.

beats.say: How long would you last on top of Everest without oxygen? You're at 8,848.86 meters. Each breath holds one-third the oxygen.
beats.img: a lone climber silhouette seen from behind on a narrow snowy summit ridge above a sea of clouds, deep blue thin sky, harsh bright sun

beats.say: In January it averages -36 °C up here. Winds blow over 160 km/h. You breathe faster and get less.
beats.img: violent wind tearing a long plume of ice crystals off a jagged Himalayan peak, frozen rock and blue ice glittering in cold sunlight

beats.say: Arrive this fast and the FAA says useful consciousness can go in 30 seconds. Not death. Just no clear thinking.
beats.img: a snowy mountain horizon tilting and blurring at the edges of vision, the bright white glare dimming into a dark tunnel

beats.say: At 28,000 ft, the upper end is 1.5 minutes. Impairment starts at once.
beats.img: a steep icy slope dropping away below a bootprint trail in fresh snow, ropes fading into blowing spindrift, no one in sight

beats.say: Slow onset gives 2.5 to 3 minutes. That's for a resting, unacclimatized person who can still act.
beats.img: a single ice axe planted upright in wind-packed summit snow at dusk, long blue shadows and a curved horizon of endless peaks

gumi.say: Gumi's odds: one percent. Real climbers acclimatize for weeks and usually bring bottled oxygen.
